flux_calibrator.value: SMA: Uranus (disk model) as bandpass, gain and flux calibrator; ALMA: Uranus flux, J2333-237 bandpass, J0137-245 phase/amplitude

evidence.quote: We used the nearby ($\sim$20$^\circ$ from NGC 253) planet Uranus as bandpass, gain and absolute flux calibrator.
Uranus was used as absolute flux calibrator, J2333-237 as a bandpass calibrator and J0137-245 as phase and amplitude calibrator.
The accuracy of the flux calibration is estimated to be within 30% at 690 GHz and $\sim$20% at 345 GHz.
Using the strong continuum emission, self-calibration was applied to the phases to improve the image quality of the continuum and line maps.

analysis_steps.goal: LVG excitation modelling of CO ladder

method.value: RADEX grid with reduced chi2 minimization; one- and two-temperature models for disk, east and west shells

evidence.quote: We conducted an LVG analysis with the RADEX code (cite: vdt07) applying a reduced $\chi^2$ minimization method

key_parameters.value: Tkin 10-400 K (10 K steps), nH2 1e3-1e8, NCO 1e14-1e19 (0.1 dex), dv=100 km/s, uniform sphere; acceptable chi2_red<=1.5; cold component <=150 K

evidence.quote: All reduced $\chi^2_{\rm red}$ results for which the modelled line ratios are within at least $\sim$1-1.5$\sigma$ of the observed line ratios (i.e., $\chi^2_{\rm red}\leq1.5$) were considered as acceptable solutions.
applying a reduced $\chi^2$ minimization method to fit the basic excitation conditions of the molecular gas in the western and eastern shells and the (averaged) disk.
This is in agreement with previous findings on the CO line SED of NGC 253 by different groups based on single-dish and/or satellite ( *Herschel*) observations (cite: ros14; hail08).

findings_qualitative.value: 12CO(6-5) follows the distribution of lower-J CO along the disk with little ratio variation; only marginal emission at the shells

evidence.quote: Only marginal $^{12}$CO(J=6–5)  emission is detected in the vicinity of the expanding shells at the eastern and western edges of the disk.

claims.hypothesis: Does 12CO(6-5) trace the same gas as lower-J CO along the disk?
claims.experiment: Compared mosaics, spectra and brightness temperature ratios of four CO transitions at matched resolution
claims.result: Distributions and line profiles resemble each other with small ratio variations
claims.finding: All transitions trace the same molecular clumps

evidence.quote: This is strong evidence that all four transitions trace the same molecular gas

claims.hypothesis: Can a single-temperature gas reproduce the disk CO ladder?
claims.result: No one-phase solution reproduced high 6-5/1-0 ratio; two-phase ~10 K and ~340 K fits
